problem:
Find the fifth term of the sequence given by the recurrence relation

$$
{a}_{n}=2{a}_{n-1}-3,\,{a}_{1}=5,\,n\ge 2.
$$

feedback.problem:
Find the fourth term of the sequence given by the recurrence relation

$$
{a}_{n}=\frac{1}{2}{a}_{n-1}+\frac{1}{3}{a}_{n-2},\,{a}_{1}=6,\,{a}_{2}=3,\,n\ge 3.
$$
feedback.worked_solution:
Starting with the initial terms ${a}_{1}=6,$ and ${a}_{2}=3,$ we compute the next terms using the recursive formula until we reach the fourth term.

$$
\begin{aligned}{a}_{1} & =6 \\ {a}_{2} & =3 \\ {a}_{3} & =\frac{1}{2}{a}_{2}+\frac{1}{3}{a}_{1}=\frac{1}{2}\cdot 3+\frac{1}{3}\cdot 6=\frac{3}{2}+2=\frac{7}{2} \\ {a}_{4} & =\frac{1}{2}{a}_{3}+\frac{1}{3}{a}_{2}=\frac{1}{2}\cdot \frac{7}{2}+\frac{1}{3}\cdot 3=\frac{7}{4}+1=\frac{11}{4}\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, the fourth term is ${a}_{4}=\frac{11}{4}.$
